hook_text: Seven hundred young people with pistols against an army with tanks. They knew they would lose. They fought anyway.
clip_script: Warsaw, 1940. The Germans build a wall around the Jewish neighbourhood and lock more than 400 000 people inside. Children sneak through holes to smuggle bread. In 1942 the trains begin. About 265 000 people are taken to Treblinka and murdered. The young people who are left make a choice. Their leader, Mordechaj Anielewicz, is twenty-three. On 19 April 1943 the German army marches in. It is met with gunfire and petrol bombs, and it retreats. So the Germans burn the ghetto, street by street. The fighters hold out for almost four weeks. Two years later the tide has turned: Stalingrad, El Alamein, D-Day. On 8 May 1945, Germany surrenders. But the fighters of Warsaw had already won something that day could not: they proved that people can resist.
visual_style: A wall rises across a map of Warsaw; small figures pass a loaf through a gap; flames spread across rooftops; a calendar flips to 19 April 1943; a map shows arrows closing in on Berlin; crowds celebrate under a banner reading 8 May 1945.
pacing: Steady build to the uprising, a pause, then a quicker sweep to the end of the war.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to learn how the uprising unfolded and how the war in Europe ended.
